ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows an op-amp circuit. The output is labeled V0(f). A block labeled Network B(f) takes a signal from the output side and feeds back Vf(f) to the non-inverting (+) input, forming the positive-feedback path. The inverting (−) input has a resistive negative-feedback network: R2 connects from the output node back to the inverting input node, and R1 connects from that node to the reference/ground return. Reasoning: At f0, the feedback network has B(f0) = Vf/V0 = 1/6 ∠0°. For sustained sinusoidal oscillation, the Barkhausen condition requires the loop gain A·B = 1 ∠0°, so the amplifier gain must be A = 6 ∠0°. From the shown resistor connections, the op-amp amplifier is non-inverting, so A = 1 + R2/R1. Setting 1 + R2/R1 = 6 gives R2/R1 = 5. Therefore, R2 = 5R1.
